_note: ACQUISITION PHASE CLOSED. The corpus stands at 16 gated + 29 expansion = 45 documents, inside the 40-60 target set in ROADMAP.md, so no further fetch round is planned. `candidates` is deliberately EMPTY: fetch_expansion.py refuses a plan with no candidates, so this file can no longer cause a download even if someone passes --allow-download to it. The five candidates that never arrived are recorded in _open_annex below, with what three rounds taught us about each host, so that reopening acquisition starts from evidence rather than from the same guesses.

_acquisition_record.round_1: 12 attempted, 6 fetched, 5 sealed, 1 discarded (y05 GAO: 286pp over the 250-page cap at 15.3 MB, 13x the whole corpus for one refusal branch).
_acquisition_record.totals: 25 requests, 14 documents fetched, 13 sealed, 1 discarded. Hosts that answered: nvlpubs.nist.gov 7/7, irs.gov 5/5, www.rfc-editor.org 1/4.
_acquisition_record.producers_gained: Acrobat PDFMaker for Word (generations 11, 17, 20) via Adobe PDF Library 11.0/15.0/20.9.95/20.13.106; Microsoft Word 2010 direct; pdfTeX (TeX Live 2020); Antenna House PDF Output Library 6.6 / AH XSL Formatter; Adobe LiveCycle Designer 6.5; cairo 1.16.0 via xml2rfc 3.12.10. None of these existed in the corpus before tranche 2.

_open_annex._note: Not a plan. These are the five that never arrived, kept so the knowledge is not lost. Reopening acquisition means confirming each URL against its host's own site FIRST -- every failure below was a guessed path, and guessing cost three of four RFC candidates.

rfc_pre_v3_pdfs.what_we_learned: The native path IS correct for RFCs authored in RFCXML v3: D19c fetched https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.pdf successfully, 194 pages, produced by cairo 1.16.0 via xml2rfc 3.12.10. The half of the hypothesis that held is the v3 boundary; the half that failed is the pdfrfc path, which was invented. No working URL for a pre-v3 RFC PDF has been demonstrated, and it is possible the RFC Editor simply does not publish one for text-era RFCs.
rfc_pre_v3_pdfs.before_retrying: Look up one such RFC on rfc-editor.org and read the actual link off the page. Do not guess a third scheme.
rfc_pre_v3_pdfs.value_if_recovered: low-to-moderate. The fixed-pitch ASCII-art case (rfc793) is genuinely unlike anything held; the plain-prose cases are already covered by y10 and y17.

crs_reports.what_we_tried: crsreports.congress.gov returned 403 to a declared non-browser User-Agent; everycrsreport.com returned 404 for a guessed /files/<id>.pdf scheme.
crs_reports.what_we_learned: The 403 is a User-Agent filter and is NOT to be worked around: impersonating a browser to defeat bot detection is evasion, and a test corpus is not worth it. The everycrsreport 404 is an ordinary wrong-URL, since that host publishes an open access policy; its real file naming was never established.
crs_reports.value_if_recovered: low. CRS output is Word-to-Acrobat, a dialect now represented by seven documents.

wikimedia_export.what_we_tried: 429 in round 1; 429 again in round 3 even after fetch_expansion.py began honouring Retry-After once.
wikimedia_export.what_we_learned: upload.wikimedia.org rate-limits this access pattern beyond what a single polite retry clears. Retrying harder is the wrong response to a host saying no twice.
wikimedia_export.value_if_recovered: low. It would add a CC-BY-SA document, but y17 already provides the only non-public-domain licence case the corpus needs to reason about.
